title: Sam Altman Tells Court Elon Musk Wanted Total Control of OpenAI
excerpt: In explosive testimony, the OpenAI CEO said Musk proposed passing the AI lab to his children and sought to merge it with Tesla
body:
Sam Altman took the witness stand in an Oakland federal courtroom this week and delivered testimony that could reshape the future of artificial intelligence governance. The OpenAI CEO told jurors that Elon Musk, before departing the nonprofit board in 2018, pushed repeatedly for total control of the organization — including a proposal to hand it to his children if he died.

The Power Struggle: The trial, now in its third week, pits Musk against the company he co-founded with roughly $38 million in donations. Musk alleges OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit mission by pivoting to a for-profit model now valued at an estimated $852 billion ahead of a planned IPO. He is seeking up to $180 billion in damages and the removal of Altman from leadership.

Altman pushed back forcefully. "I was opposed to AI being under the control of any one person," he testified, framing Musk's departure not as a betrayal but as a relief — one that actually boosted internal morale and freed the research team to focus on safety-first development. Earlier testimony from Shivon Zilis, a Musk associate, revealed that Musk had attempted to recruit Altman to run Tesla's AI lab, a detail that complicates Musk's narrative of being sidelined.

Why Silicon Valley Is Watching: The case is far more than a billionaire grudge match. A ruling in Musk's favor could unwind OpenAI's corporate restructuring and potentially block its IPO, sending shockwaves through the AI industry. OpenAI's co-founder Greg Brockman testified earlier that Musk himself had advocated for a for-profit entity before leaving — a claim Musk's legal team disputes. Former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, who left OpenAI last year, has separately alleged a "consistent pattern of lying" by Altman, adding further intrigue.

For Indian-American tech professionals — many of whom work at OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic, and the broader AI ecosystem — the trial's outcome could determine whether the industry's most powerful company remains on its current trajectory or faces a governance upheaval that ripples across hiring, equity, and research priorities.

What Comes Next: Closing arguments are expected Thursday. The jury will then decide whether Musk's $180 billion claim has merit — a verdict that could either validate his crusade for AI accountability or cement Altman's vision of a commercially driven safety-first lab. Either way, the precedent will matter far beyond this courtroom.
nri_angle: Thousands of Indian-American engineers work across the AI ecosystem at OpenAI, xAI, and competitors; the trial outcome could reshape hiring, equity, and governance at the industry's most valuable company.
